stages.heading: Stardate 2400.0 (Introduction)
commentary: Welcome to another map of AP Bot Solitaire. Last time we left off, we were overran by their Boarding technology. Being able to capture bigger ships with relative ease is huge when the only counter measure literally is Security Forces. Thus, we are scaling back to Easy difficulty.

Normally, when multiple AP bots are present, they operate as an Uneasy Alliance. For this playthrough, we will make an intentional deviation, and activate the Sinister ruleset. This means each player has a unique primary objective. For example, if we are to win, we must conquer Medusa's homeworld, before any other homeworld is eliminated. It also means a penalty the AP bots normally would have for out-numbering the human players (-1 home system economic roll) will remain inactive here.

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.3
commentary: Exploration is going to be a bit awkward with the amount of spacing that exists in between players.

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.6
commentary: Where did all the planets go? Looks like our economy will be dented for this opening stretch.

stages.heading: Stardate 2400.9
commentary: We finally found our first planet, but it is a bit too late, relative to the first economic phase.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.0
commentary: It could be worse; we could be down a scout this early in the journey, simply because some black hole decided to greet us. Anyway, we start with Ship Size 2 (-10), followed by 2 Colony Ships (-16) and 1 Scout (-6). This spends all of our money.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.2
commentary: It was only a matter of time before more planets started showing up.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.5
commentary: Yet... the black hole is still missing. Chances are, it will probably be among the last of the home system hexes.

stages.heading: Stardate 2401.8
commentary: Sure enough, the black hole was not very far behind. Our exploring Scout rolls a 4, escaping its gravitational pull decently.

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.0
commentary: It is not every day we make a comeback on economics. Eventually, our income will catch up to a more typical opening. To that end, we buy Ship Size 3 (-15) and 2 more Colony Ships (-16).

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.1
commentary: And thus exhausts the last of our home systems.

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.4
commentary: We go into deep space now, taking care not to accidentally activate either AP bot. We endure quite the series of misfortunes with these first hexes. Between 2 Danger markers and a Plasma Storm, that is 3 scouts already eliminated!

stages.heading: Stardate 2402.7
commentary: On the other hand, these misfortunes sharply cut our maintenance down.

stages.heading: Stardate 2403.0
commentary: How fortunate it is to be able to pay relatively little maintenance once in a while. We buy Terraforming 1 (-20) and 2 more Colony Ships (-16).

Normally, this would be the point where we start rolling dice to move cosmic storms. But, none of the newly revealed plasma storm's available moves (relative to I4) would be legal. (Our home systems and the unexplored terrain block all six sides.) Thus, we skip these steps, for now.

stages.heading: Stardate 2403.3
commentary: Not exactly a lot of options are available at this point in the journey.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.0
commentary: And thanks to that supernova, we opt to condense the rest of the economic phase. We buy Exploration 1 (-15) and Attack 1 (-20), followed by 2 Cruisers (-24).

We have reached the point in the playthrough where the AP bots start to activate, starting with their initial Exploration Vessels. Since the Sinister ruleset is active, it makes the most sense to position them such that they open up an offense path to the respective opponents. Since there are several stretches where there are just 2 deep space hexes in between home systems, that is the configuraiton that the AP bots use. Thus, their Exploration and Terraforming remain at level 0.
Finally, we decide to do the first initiative differently to discourage attempting to steal it early on. All players have rolled 6 (ourselves) / 4 (Medusa) / 1 (Cassandra). We take the initiative.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.2
commentary: While we get out Cruisers in position, the AP bots do their first adventures into deep space.

Cassandra's EV has encountered a Danger marker already, shutting down their ability to uncover a path right away. Chances are, they will have to use the Prime Directive in order to brute force their first fleet's way through.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.5
commentary: Medusa's EV was not very far behind, but at least they opened a path to Cassandra.

stages.heading: Stardate 2404.8
commentary: We finally get our own chance to explore deep space, and we do so in a relatively safe manner. This particular Danger marker's effects were negated.

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.0
commentary: This will become the most explosive economic phase as the rest of the AP bot logic awakens. Before we proceed though, we take care of our own empire. We buy Attack 2 (-30), followed by another 2 Cruisers (-24). We also build satellites (-6) to defend Cerberus. We also start placing our free Light Infantry.
{prodTable}{techTable}

Now that both AP bots are fully awake, we proceed with their economic rolls. Medusa has rolled 4,5,5,5,5/10. Cassandra has rolled 3,4,6/9,10,10. On the Exploration step, these bots have rolled 52 (Medusa) / 24 (Cassandra). Since both bots passed this paranoia check, no investment takes place.
On the bid step, they rolled 86 (Medusa) / 84 (Cassandra). Both passed, so no bids take palce.

Since their Terraforming is capped at level 0, it sharply simplifies steps related to it. They will never automatically launch a fleet. Thus, they rolled 10 (Medusa) / 8 (Cassandra) for fleet launches. The former built a forward operating base, instead of launching a fleet.

Cassandra did launch a fleet. Since technology CP is plentiful at first, they buy Movement 2 right away (-20). They then rolled a 9 (failure >3), so that ends this step. Finally, since they have no FOB of their own, they place their fleet at their homeworld.

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.1
commentary: Now that the most explosive segment is out of the way, we can now resume our journey in earnest.

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.4
commentary: A pleasantly surprising sequence of events! We unveiled a space wreck!

stages.heading: Stardate 2405.7
commentary: And now a regional map gives us even more information!

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.0
commentary: Economic Phase break time! We use this opportunity to buy Movement 2 (-20), followed by 2 more Cruisers (-24) at the homeworld, and also a Base (-12) at Cerberus.
{prodTable}{techTable}
Things have become a little dicier now that Cassandra has their first fleet on the board. Still, their available economic rolls are 2,3,4,6,7,8 (Medusa) / 1,2,3,10,10 (Cassandra).
For Exploration and bidding, they rolled 86,26 (Medusa) / 19,79 (Cassandra), respectively. All of these paranoia checks passed.

For fleet launches, they rolled 5 (Medusa) / 3 (Cassandra). Both AP bots launch fresh expansion fleets, and buy their respective Movement technology right away. They then rolled 4 (Medusa) / 1 (Cassandra), causing the latter to double down on this investment. Finally, since Medusa has a FOB, they conduct one last paranoia check. A 20 (pass), allowing them to place their newest fleet at their FOB.
Finally, since no bids took place, we take advantage of the fact that we win the tiebreaker, and use it to transfer the initiative to Medusa.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.3
commentary: Once again, Cassandra effectively runs into a bottleneck with deep space.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.6
commentary: Unlike last time though, both of their expansion fleets are unidentified. Thus, we override the scenario book via prime directive now, and use their oldest fleet to uncover a hex anyway... at the expense of weakening that fleet a bit (-6 CP worth of ships).

Since our forces threaten Medusa's territory, their fleet assumes defense posture, and goes after our forces. We also end our movement inside Medusa's territory, necessitating a random encounter roll is made. A 5, so none appeared.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.9A (The Battle for Cerberus)
commentary: An opportunity presents itself where they can combine two fleets in order to assault our colony with a larger fleet. Since this is Cassandra's first battle, they rolled a 91 for fleet strategy. This gives them the Yarr strategy. This fleet is also against one of our colonies, so they potentially factor transports in their equation. The available CP is spent as follows:
1. A 7 was rolled on the random counter tech step. Securing Forces 1 (70 → 55 tech CP)
• A 50 was rolled on the paranoia check (pass). Troops 2 (55 → 45 tech CP)
• Boarding 1 (45 → 25 tech CP)
• Defense 1 (25 → 5 tech CP)
• Security Forces does not require any particular ship, so counter tech ships step is skipped
• 1x Transport (114 → 108 combined assigned CP)
• 5x Space Marines + 1x Heavy Infantry (108 → 96 assigned CP)
• 8x Boarding Ships (96 → 0 assigned CP)

Already this is not a good sign. The good news is that we have far fewer bodies (specifically, just 2 cruisers) for them to even capture, in addition to a pair of immobile bodies that are immune to capture.
1. Space Round 1: Cassandra screens their transport each round, if able
• Our available ships have the best weapon class, so we go first. Since only their boarding ships are fair game at present, our Base rolled a 9 (≤8 to hit)
• Our Defense Satellite Network rolled an 8 (≤5 to hit)
• Our 2 Cruisers rolled 7,8 (0 hits ≤5)
• Their Boarding Ships are next. Our Cruisers are capturable, so they rolled 9,6,7,7,1,10,3,5 accordingly (2 hits ≤3)
• Space Round 2: Our Base rolled a 2 against their boarding ships (hit ≤8)
• Our Satellites rolled a 9 (≤5 to hit)
• Cassandra took no damage last round, so they skip the morale check (as if it passed)
• Their 2 Cruisers are currently recovering from the capture process. They are unable to shoot this round
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 6,1,10,7,7,2,10,5 against our satellites (1 hits ≤1). Note that these satellites are immune, so they simply damage them
• Space Round 3: Our Base rolled a 5 against their boarding ships (hit ≤8)
• Our Satellites rolled a 2 (hit ≤5)
• Cassandra took relatively minor damage last round. Thus, they rolled a 65 for morale (pass >5), allowing them to stay
• Their 2 Cruisers have finished the capture process. They rolled 1/5 (1 hit ≤5/4), knocking out our satellites
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 3,6,7,8,8,9,10 against our base (0 hits ≤1)
• Space Round 4: Our Base rolled a 5 against their cruisers (hit ≤8)
• Cassandra lost a ship last round. Thus, they rolled a 15 for morale (failure ≤26), causing them to begin retreat procedures
• Still, their 2 Cruisers shoot one last time. They rolled 6,10 (0 hits ≤4)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 1,2,4,5,6,7,9 against our base (1 hit ≤1)
• Space Round 5: Our Base rolled a 4 against their cruisers (hit ≤8), finishing one off
• Since Cassandra previously failed a morale check, their fleet retreats from the space battle
• Ground Round 1: Despite the fiasco though, Cassandra did land their ground forces. They will need a round to get settled though
• Our 5 Militia rolled 7,1,10,1/6, prioritizing their sole heavy infantry (1 hit ≤3/4)
• Ground Round 2: Their Space Marines have settled, and rolled 4,6,7,9,10 (2 hits ≤6)
• Our Militia rolled 7,8,9 (0 hits ≤4)
• Ground Round 3: Their Space Marines have rolled 2,2,4,5,6 (5 hits ≤6), eliminating the last of the defenders
...  and, thus, capturing this planet. One of their space marines has been consumed to install a new government. Our Base has been destroyed by their orbital weaponry.

stages.heading: Stardate 2406.9P (The Battle for Eccles)
commentary: We now move our offensive fleet and assault the planet of Eccles. Before we proceed with bombardment though, we need to conduct another random encounter. A 9 was rolled, causing them to spend 30 CP to build defensive ships.

Their fleet bank is empty, so those points are drawn out of the Technology bank to replace the shortage. Additionally, because this is Medusa's first battle; we proceed with rolling for their fleet strategy, even though technology spending typically does not take place. A 62 was rolled, causing them to go for the Hit and Run strategy.
1. Ship Size 2 (90 → 80 tech CP)
• Ship Size 3 (80 → 65 tech CP)
• A 3 was rolled on the upgrade step. Attack 1 was bought (65 → 45 tech CP)
• Ship Size 4 (45 → 25 tech CP)
• Fastmove 1 (25 → 15 tech CP)
• 2x Battlecruiser (30 → 0 assigned CP)
• A 2 was rolled for ground units (2 light infantry placed)
Now that their forces are assembled, we proceed to battle.
1. Round 1: Medusa's newly developed Battlecruisers have the best weapon class, so they shoot first. They rolled 8,7 against our scout (0 hits ≤6)
• Our ships have rolled 7,2/9 (1 hit ≤5/2)

• Round 2: Not only has Medusa taken some damage, the mere fact that their battlecruisers are even present causes a considerable spike in the morale threshold (comparable to having lost a ship in battle)
• Thus, they rolled a 17 for morale (failure ≤26), causing their Battlecruisers to immediately retreat from battle
• Bombardment Round: Our ships are now clear to bombard, having rolled 4,4/2 (3 hits ≤5/2). This colony is already destroyed!

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.0
commentary: What an exceptionally chaotic set of turns that have taken place! Before we can do any spending, we should roll on a space wreck we cashed in recently. A 2 was rolled this way, giving us Ship Size 4.

Moving right along, we place a bid of 9 to allow for a very high chance to retake the initiative. We also buy Ship Yards 2 (-20), and use the newly increased capacity to build 6 Scouts (-36) and also an extra homeworld Ship Yard (-6).
{prodTable}{techTable}

AP Bot economics have become a lot more dynamic. Their available economic rolls are 6,6,9,9 (Medusa) and 3,5,6,6,9/4 (Cassandra). Notice that one of Cassandra's deep space rolls is distinguished from the rest, having been acquired from capturing our planet.
For Exploration, they rolled 69 (Medusa) / 18 (Cassandra). These paranoia checks passed.

For bidding, Cassandra rolled a 74 (Cassandra). Since Medusa's assets are currently being besieged, they automatically fail this paranoia check. They rolled 5,7, and add a net paranoia modifier of zero. They place a bid of 5.

For fleet launches, they rolled 6 (Medusa) / 3 (Cassandra). Both players launch new fleets. For various reasons, fleet placement is limited exclusively to the homeworlds. Also, their respective tech banks are small (<60 CP), so they skip the Movement step.

Finally, since we won the bid; we used this opportunity to retake the initiative. This is also the first economic phase in which the plasma storm is no longer trapped. It rolled a 7, causing it to remain stationary.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.2
commentary: Since our oldest fleet never got its Movement equipment upgraded, we opt to bow out of Medusa's space... for the moment.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.5 (The Bombardment of Antares)
commentary: Cassandra has reached another planet of ours. Since they have no ground units left, they simply proceed with bombardment. Their ships rolled 8/2,4,4,4,6,8,9,10 (0 hits ≤6/1), dealing no meaningful damage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2407.8
commentary: This will be one of our busier turns.
The Battle for Cobol
During our turn, we assault the NPA planet of Cobol. After uncovering their 4 ships, we proceed accordingly.
1. Round 1: The NPA has the tactics advantage, so their Alien-Cs go first. They rolled 5/9, prioritizing our lone scout (1 hit ≤5/4)
• Our Cruisers have differing Attack equipment. Still, we rolled a 4 against their Alien-D (hit ≤5), 2/1 against their Alien-Cs (2 hits ≤4/3), and an 8 against their Alien-E (≤4 to hit)
• Their Alien-E rolled a 6 hit (hit ≤6)
• Round 2: Our Cruisers gain the Fleet Size Bonus, and rolled 4,7/6,1 (2 hits ≤6/5), finishing off the NPA and subduing this planet
The Battle for Cerberus
Cassandra proceeds to battle our blockading scouts. Since their tech bank is empty, they keep their fleet strategy, and build another 5 Boarding Ships.
1. Round 1: Our Scouts have the best weapon class, and shoot first. We rolled 1,2,4,6,9,10 (2 hits ≤3)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 5,7,7,9 (0 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our Scouts rolled 1,2,3,4,5,6 (3 hits ≤3)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled an 84 for morale (pass >16), followed by 2,7,7 (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 3: Our Scouts rolled a 3 against the scout they took from us (hit ≤4), followed by 3,4,4,6 (1 hit ≤3)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled a 20 for morale (failure ≤50), causing the surviving ships to retreat from this battle
The Bombardment of Antares
The bombardment against our planet of Antares continues. Cassandra rolls 5/1,1,2,5,6,8,9,10 (3 hits ≤6/1), glassing this colony thanks to a burst of luck.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.0
commentary: Overall, Cassandra is causing our economy to falter. Combined with the fact that Medusa is not exerting pressure on them, it is not exactly helping us.

This time, we opt to forgo bidding, as recent studies have unveiled a suggestion we can try using against boarding ships. Thus, we will buy Fighter 1 (-25), followed by a full Carrier (-27) and an extra homeworld Ship Yard (-6).
From an organization standpoint, it is simplest to conduct the plasma storm's movement here. It rolled a 9, causing it to be still once more.
{prodTable}{techTable}

Both AP bots are also faltering a bit on economics. Cassandra because we blockaded the colony they captured from us (though we did cause them to have a shattered fleet); and Medusa because they have 2 active fleets and are still missing a colony. Thus, their rolls this time are just 4,4,7 (Medusa) / 1,1,2,6,10 (Cassandra).
Medusa's home systems are now clear. They buy a Colony Ship (-8).
For Exploration, they rolled 3 (Medusa) / 40 (Cassandra). Medusa failed this paranoia check, and bought Exploration 1 (-15).

For bidding, both AP bots' assets are threatened, so they automatically place bids. Cassandra rolled 5,6 (placing a bid of 3). Medusa rolled 7,9 (placing a bid of 7). This process causes Medusa to go first.

For fleet launches, we believe Medusa should not attempt this sequence with <30 CP available in both banks combined, unless it is able to merge the shattered fleet right away. As it is false, this leaves only Cassandra with being eligible. They rolled a 9, a failure. Thus, they build a Forward Operating Base, instead of a new fleet.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.1 (The Battle for Sector G11)
commentary: While Medusa chases us, Cassandra conducts a paranoia check (1 fleet threatened). A 3, which fails (≤9).

During our turn, we opt to send our Cruisers into battle against one of Medusa's hidden fleets. Since their fleet strategy was previously known from a random encounter, and that their tech bank is almost gone, they simply build 4 battlecruisers (-60).
1. Round 1: Medusa has the weapon class advantage, so their Battlecruisers go first. They rolled 2,2,3,3, prioritizing our newer cruisers (4 hits ≤5)
• Since they easily eliminated our differences, our remaining Cruisers simply rolled 2,7 (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 2: Since one of Medusa's Battlecruisers are damaged, they rolled a 26 for morale (pass >9). They then take advantage of the Fleet Size Bonus, and rolled 1,8,9,9 (1 hit ≤6)
• Our Cruisers rolled 2,7 (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 3: Medusa's Battlecruisers have rolled a 68 for morale (pass >26). They lost the FSB though, and rolled 2,6,9 (1 hit ≤5)
• Our last Cruiser rolled a 3 (hit ≤4)
• Round 4: Medusa's Battlecruisers have rolled a 54 for morale (pass >26). They regain the FSB, and rolled 6,7,9 (1 hit ≤6)
• Our Cruiser rolled a 2 (hit ≤4)
• Round 5: Medusa's Battlecruisers have rolled a 33 for morale (pass >26). They keep the FSB, and rolled 1,10 (1 hit ≤6), finishing our cruisers off

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.4
commentary: Overall, Medusa netted a tactical victory. They eliminated our fleet, but the sufficient loss of key ships has caused their paranoia level to remain the same. Their 2 fleets also merge, and their new total (140 CP worth) causes them to become to an extermination fleet.

stages.heading: Stardate 2408.7 (The Battle for Omicron)
commentary: Cassandra has now reached another decision where a paranoia check is necessary. A 51 was rolled (pass >9), allowing them to contest a colony. Since they still have our Movement 1 cruiser, they are limited to a colony that is also guarded.
1. Round 1: Our Fighters have the weapon class advantage, so we go first. Focusing on their cruiser, we rolled 10,1,10 (1 hit ≤5)
• Their Cruiser rolled a 1 against our fighters (hit ≤6)
• Our Carrier and Scouts rolled 7,9,2/3,9,10 against their cruiser/boarding ships (2 hits ≤3)
• Their Transport rolled a 1 against our fighters (hit ≤1)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 3,6,6,8,8,8,8 against our scouts (1 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Our last Fighter has rolled 6 against the scout that was just captured (hit ≤6)
• Our Carrier and Scouts rolled 1,3,5,6,8 against their boarding ships (2 hits ≤3)
• Their Transport is screened this round
• Their Boarding Ships rolled a 46 for morale (pass >37), and rolled 5,5,6,8,9,10 against our scouts (0 hits ≤4)
• Round 3: Our Fighter has rolled 6 against their boarding ships (≤5 to hit)
• Our Carrier and Scouts rolled 1,3,6,9,9 against their boarding ships (2 hits ≤3)
• Their Transport is screened this round
• Their Boarding Ships rolled a 4 for morale (failure ≤62), and begin retreat procedures. They refuse to abandon their transport (yet), and rolled 4,6,6,8,9 against our scouts anyway (1 hit ≤4)
• Round 4: Our Fighter has rolled a 9 against the scout that was just captured (≤6 to hit)
• Our Carrier and Scouts rolled 7,9,7,5 against the scout (0 hits ≤4)
• Their entire fleet retreats from this battle, having failed the morale check last round

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.0
commentary: We were able to hold steady this time. Fighters seems to be the better answer against boarding ships, given that they are immune to capture. We also are no longer exerting pressure on Medusa at the moment, allowing them to start threatening Cassandra.
We buy 2 full carriers (-54) at the homeworld, followed by a Base (-12) at Omicron.
The plasma storm rolls a 10, causing it to remain stationary yet again.
{prodTable}{techTable}
AP Bot economics are recovering a bit. Their home system economic rolls are 3,4,8,10 (Medusa) / 3,3,6,7,10 (Cassandra). Cassandra also rolls a 3 for its deep space economics.
For Exploration, they rolled 34 (Medusa) / 30 (Cassandra). Both AP bots pass this paranoia check.

For bidding, Medusa rolls a 7. Since both AP bots have failed (or will auto-fail) this paranoia check, they place bids. Medusa rolled 1,8 (placing a bid of 1). Cassandra rolled 1,10 (placing a bid of 2). This process causes Cassandra to go first.

For fleet launches, they rolled 5 (Medusa) / 10 (Cassandra). Only Medusa launches a fresh fleet. They conduct one last paranoia check, having rolled a 91 (pass). They place their newest fleet at their FOB. Since Cassandra did not launch a fleet, they instead build a FOB at the captured colony they recently freed from our blockade.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.3
commentary: Before Cassandra circles around for a rematch, it must conduct a paranoia check for posture. A 6 was rolled (failure ≤26), causing their oldest fleet to assume defense posture.
Meanwhile, Medusa is able to merge again, further strengthening their extermination fleet. They may be able to win this game.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.6
commentary: Cassandra's oldest fleet is no longer threatened (we opted to hold position and consolidate), so it assumes offense posture once more.

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.9A (The Bombardment of Sheldon)
commentary: Once again, Cassandra must make a paranoia check. This time, a 59 was rolled (pass). Since it has encountered Fighter technology in battle and is unable to counter it, it proceeds to the lightly defended planet of Sheldon.
Their ships have rolled 2/1,2,2,5,9,9 (2 hits ≤3/1)

stages.heading: Stardate 2409.9P (The Battle for Sheldon)
commentary: They damaged our next colony, but not destroyed it. We swoop in with our fleet, and use them against theirs.
1. Round 1: Our Fighters have the weapon class advantage once more. Focusing on their scout/boarding ships, we rolled 2/10,7,5,2,4,2 (5 hits ≤6/5)
• Their Transport rolled a 5 against our fighters (≤1 to hit)
• Our Carriers and Scouts rolled 9,4,9,1,1,9 against their boarding ships (2 hits ≤3)
• Their Boarding Ships rolled 3,10 against our scouts (1 hits ≤4)
• Round 2: Having gained the FSB, our Fighters rolled 9,2/3,6,7,5,3 against their scout/boarding ships (5 hits ≤7/6)
• Their Transport is all alone now. Cassandra has endured massive losses, causing a morale threshold of 91. Thus, it rolls a 31, and retreats from this battle
During Medusa's turn, they invade Cassandra's space. A 3 was rolled for random encounters, none take place.

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.0
commentary: Our economy took some more damage, but it could be worse. We shattered Cassandra's oldest fleet in circulation.
Incidentally, we have exactly enough production for another 2 full carriers (-54), so we buy them.
The plasma storm rolls a 3, causing it to jump through the fold in space and meet up with the asteroid belt.
{prodTable}{techTable}
AP Bots are holding steady. Their home system economic rolls are 1,2,4,9 (Medusa) / 1,2,3,4,7,9 (Cassandra). Cassandra also rolls a 10 for its deep space economics.
For Exploration, they rolled 75 (Medusa) / 14 (Cassandra). Cassandra fails this paranoia check, and buys Exploration 1 (-15).

For bidding, both AP bots are technically threatened, so they proceed accordingly. Medusa rolled 3,3, causing additional dice to be rolled. The extra bid rolls are a 2, for a total bid of 5 CP (paranoia plays no role when doubles are involved). Cassandra rolled 2,5 (placing a bid of 5). Cassandra currently has the initiative, so it wins this tie.

For fleet launches, they rolled 7 (Medusa) / 4 (Cassandra). Both launch fresh fleets. Medusa conducts one last paranoia check to determine its fleet placement. A 28 (pass), allowing it to use its FOB. Cassandra automatically fails this check, because its home systems are being invaded.

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.2 (The Battle for Eden)
commentary: Medusa is now ready to assault Eden. Before it proceeds though, it should build its remaining ships (given that it has no tech CP left). First, a paranoia check is used to determine whether transports should be built. A 65 was rolled (pass >16), causing them to build 2 Transports (-12) and 12 Light Infantry (-20). The remaining  137 assigned CP is good for 9 more battlecruisers (-135).
Afterwards, Cassandra rolls for random encounters. A 1 was rolled, so none appeared. A 10 was then rolled for ground units, giving them 4 heavy infantry.
1. Round 1: Medusa needs time for its 12 Light Infantry to settle
• Cassandra's ground forces rolled 1,3,9,10/4,6,8,8,8 (3 hits ≤5/4)
• Round 2: Cassandra's Heavy Infantry rolled 1,7,8,10 (1 hit ≤5)
• Medusa's Light Infantry rolled 10,6,3,1,10,5,1,5 (5 hits ≤5), cleaning up the militia exactly
• Round 3: Cassandra's Heavy Infantry rolled 2,3,9,9 (2 hits ≤5)
• Medusa's Light Infantry rolled 1,2,7,8,9,9 (2 hits ≤3)
• Round 4: Cassandra's Heavy Infantry rolled 1,1,3 (3 hits ≤5)
• Medusa's Light Infantry rolled 2,4,4 (1 hit ≤3)
• Round 5: Cassandra's Heavy Infantry rolled 5,7,7 (1 hit ≤5)
• Medusa's Light Infantry rolled 2,6 (1 hit ≤3)
• Round 6: Cassandra's Heavy Infantry rolled 1,2 (2 hits ≤5), successfully defending their planet

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.5A (The Battle for Eden)
commentary: Cassandra is now able to defend Eden from its aggressors. Before it proceeds though, it should build its ships (20 tech CP is neither sufficient for a fleet strategy change, nor is it sufficient for Boarding 2). The 85 assigned CP is spent exclusively on Boarding Ships (-84).
1. Round 1: Medusa's Battlecruisers have the best weapon class, so they go first. They rolled 1,1,1,2,3,5,7,8,8,8,9 (6 hits ≤5)
• Cassandra's Boarding Ships rolled 1,8,9,9 against the battlecruisers (1 hit ≤3)
• Round 2: Medusa's Battlecruisers rolled an 83 for morale (pass >16); followed by 1,7,3/4,8,8,10,1,1,3 (6 hits ≤6), focusing down on the ship that was just captured
• Cassandra's Boarding Ships rolled a 4 for morale (failure ≤84), causing them to retreat from this battle

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.5P (The Battle for Sector A3)
commentary: The recent battle victory decreases Medusa's paranoia, making the next check easier to pass (16 → 9). A 6 was rolled, causing it to fail anyway. This causes the newer expansion fleet to be stationary in defense posture, while the older extermination fleet keeps its offense posture and makes a sweeping advance. For random encounters, a 10 was rolled, causing an extra boarding ship to enter the equation.
1. Round 1: Medusa's Battlecruisers have rolled 1,3,3,4,5,8,9,9,9,10 (5 hits ≤6)
• Cassandra's Boarding Ships rolled 2,8,10 against the battlecruisers (1 hit ≤3)
• Round 2: Medusa's Battlecruisers rolled a 22 for morale (pass >16); followed by 4,4/2,3,3,9,6,8,7 (6 hits ≤6), wiping the rest of the fleet out

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.8P (The Battle for Cerberus)
commentary: We proceed to contest the planet of Cerberus once more. Since a FOB is present, they unveil a Base to compliment whatever little protectio the planet currently has.
1. Round 1: Their Base has the best weapon class, so it goes first. It rolled a 6 against our fighters (hit ≤7)
• Our Fighters rolled 5/4,4,7,10,4,6,7,1,3,1,1 (7 hits ≤5/4), utterly pulverizing their orbital protection and exposing the planet again

stages.heading: Stardate 2410.8A (The Battle for Terra)
commentary: And now for the beginning of the end. Medusa has an open path to Cassandra's homeworld, and assaults it accordingly. A 4 was rolled for ground units, generating 2 Heavy Infantry.
1. Round 1: Cassandra's Base rolls a 9 against the battlecruisers (≤6 to hit)
• Medusa's Battlecruisers rolled 1,2,2,3,5,6,7,9,10 (4 hits ≤3), wiping out the base

• Bombardment Round: The planet is completely exposed. Medusa's ships rolled 2,3,3,4,4,7,8,9,9/5,9 (5 hits ≤5/1). Assuming we revert to the pre-AGT homeworld durability (currently being discussed), then this homeworld is destroyed

stages.heading: Stardate 2411.0 (Game Over)
commentary: And thus ends this playthrough in defeat. Invading Medusa's home systems too early probably backfired on us. This process eventually caused their fleets to combine into a size worthy of an extermination fleet, and go straight for Cassandra's throat; unfazed by any paranoia checks that may fail. Combined with how [un]successful Boarding Ships were against battlecruisers, this ultimately gave Medusa a decisive victory.

Still, we gave the Sinister ruleset a shot. Mileage may vary on whether or not this is a good fit for AP Bot games. Nonetheless, the AP Bot system still has plenty of potential. We plan on peeling off a few layers at a time still while learning the many intricacies and ironing out mistakes.
